doc.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021

title: Jon Hendricks and vocal accompaniment
summary: Hendricks was a natural improviser; Weiss worked in his quartet-plus-singers set and comments on accompanying vocalists.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Excellent. I wanted to run a couple of names by you. We already talked about Joe Wilder. And maybe you have something you can offer on Jon Hendricks?

Well Jon had good taste in a lot of things. He liked to live well. He was a complete natural and he’s probably one of the very very few vocalists who could improvise a jazz solo on par with any horn player. He really knew the language. He really got it. And when I worked with him he had four singers, it was like an expanded Lambert, Hendricks & Ross type of repertoire, but every set included at least two or three songs just quartet with Jon and the rhythm section. And that was very very satisfying and enjoyable because it was just like playing a quartet with a tenor saxophonist.
Is vocal accompaniment the challenging — a different sort of playing for you?

I don’t do it that much. Actually I don’t have a whole lot of experience like some pianists, working with vocalists. But I’d like to think the same criteria are in play you know, with a vocalist singing a ballad or a tenor saxophonist singing a ballad through their horn.
